title: The state of New Orleans jazz and the European trip
summary: Lee laments the loss of old New Orleans jazz and recalls his European trip with Mezz Mezzrow and Zutty Singleton; Russell asks about the French band.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: But, there was no happy days in the world of playing like the good old New Orleans days. When they had that good old real ragtime funky jazz music day. But the funny thing Bill, New Orleans ain't got it no more. They ain't got the jazz. I don't know. Young kids, young boys don't look like they go, they don't want to fall in those timers shoes. They don't play that kind of music. They have a different style. But the other boys, like my boy Tony Peretti, another good boy, they all trying to carry the traditional New Orleans on. They're all trying to go for that jazz band. And I really think that true jazz music is great old American music will never get old. Oh, sorry. Never get old. And my, what a good feeling in my life, with my wife right there, little Mary, little Mary. Oh, now I got a chance to go to Europe. Oh, yes. That European trip was a great experience for me. He played with Mez and who else was in the band? Mez Row. Zutty Singleton, the great jazz that I think would always say, regardless of his disposition, he's the greatest jazz drummer in the world. But Zutty, I want to hear some old, did you hear any old records I made with Mez? Uh-huh.
I was doing a drive, and then my help fill my ten bands, going from voice to voice.
What band you play with in France? Uh-huh. The French boys.
Well, you're going to the band that you played with there in France, with men, the musicians in the band. Is that Claude Luther or which band?
